rule-recipe-best-tornado.title: Best simulation of a tornado's parent storm for each card size
rule-recipe-best-tornado.method: Start at the 00, 06, 12 or 18 UTC analysis at least 6 hours before the tornado, so storms form in the model from the morning environment, and run until 3 hours after it ends, at least 12 hours. Put a 1 km grid over the tornado path and 120 km back along it, where the parent storm forms, with a margin of 250, 200, 150, 110, 80 or 60 km, inside a 3 km grid that reaches 400 to 180 km beyond it. From HRRR, itself a 3 km analysis, the 3 km grid is the outer one. From ERA5 (about 31 km), a 12 km grid reaching 500 km beyond the 3 km one carries the large-scale flow, so the 3 km grid is not driven straight from 31 km boundaries; every row checks at least 400 km on the fitted grids. When no 1 km grid fits, the 3 km grid runs alone (inside the 12 km one for ERA5), 1100, 800 or 650 km wide, then a single 4 km grid. Each card takes the first rung the engine fits on it with at least 5% of its memory to spare and whose download, preparation, history, kept checkpoint and pictures fit the card's disk budget (40, 50, 60, 80 and 100 GiB for 8 to 32 GB) with the nests writing every 15, 20 or 30 minutes.

rule-recipe-time-estimate.title: Run time of a recipe that has not been run
rule-recipe-time-estimate.method: A forecast's time grows with its grid points and its time steps: each grid's points (east by north by levels) divided by its spacing in km, summed over the grids, times the hours. The measured runs give the seconds per unit of that for each kind of storm, on the card they ran on; a recipe that has not run gets that rate times its own grids and hours. The time to all pictures adds the download and preparation and the pictures. The download is this layout's own, as the engine prices it, over the throughput measured on real downloads of the same source; the preparation is at the rate measured on real preparations of the same kind, per byte downloaded for HRRR, whose preparation decodes every file it downloads, and per grid cell and forcing time for ERA5; the pictures are the measured seconds per picture frame per grid point times this layout's frames (each grid's history files) and points.

ideal.text: A 688 by 606 km grid at 1 km holds the tornado path and the ground 120 km back along it where the parent storm forms, so the supercell and its mesocyclone are resolved at 2023-03-25 00:57 UTC; the 3 km grid around it reaches 400 km further out for the inflow and the boundaries the storm feeds on.

cards.source_why: HRRR analysis: the 3 km analysis with radar data assimilated, archived for dates from late 2014.

physics.why: HRRR's own microphysics family (Thompson), so the storms and ice already in its analysis carry straight over, with full radiation for the evening and night hours; the engine's own default for HRRR. No cumulus scheme on any grid: every grid here resolves deep convection itself.

cards.disk_basis: the download, 14.1 GiB of HRRR files for 13 forcing times; the preparation, 2.5 GiB; the history files, 2.4 GiB, written every hour on the outer grid; the one checkpoint the run keeps (two while a new one is written), 1.1 GiB; the rendered pictures, 0.8 GiB; as the engine projects them (gpuwm/disk_budget.py, gpuwm/download_budget.py) from sizes measured on real runs; within this card's 40 GiB disk budget
cards.est_basis: estimated from the speed of 2 measured runs of this kind of storm on an RTX 5070 Ti (16 GB), scaled by this layout's grid points, time steps and hours; a faster or slower card changes it; the time to all pictures adds the download (15.2 GB of HRRR files, about 7 minutes at the 39 MB/s measured on 4 downloads of that source on the same machine) and the preparation (about 2 minutes, at the rate measured on 4 preparations of the same kind) and the pictures, about 1 minutes, scaled from the measured run that drew its pictures by this layout's picture frames and grid points
cards.why: A 3 km grid, 650 by 650 km, lets storms form on their own; it shows where and when supercells form but not their inner structure.
cards.what_is_given_up: No 1 km grid: the storm runs at 3 km, which shows the supercell but not its rotation; the grid is 650 by 650 km.
